traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full: flowers perfect, regular, in cymes or heads; calyx-tube coherent with the ovary, its limb 4 small teeth or none; petals 4, epigynous; stamens 4, alternate with the petals; ovary 2-celled. The calyx tube is wholly joined to the ovary, so no floral cup stands above it.

traits.woodiness.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 43 Cornaceae: trees, shrubs or rarely perennial herbs; leaves opposite or alternate, simple; stipules absent; fruit a drupe or berry.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 384, family Cornaceae: leaf incision none (rarely pinnatifid), usually; read as {"none": "usually"}.

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 384, family Cornaceae: stipules false, usually; read as {"false": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 384, family Cornaceae: inflorescence cyme (or head of cymes, rarely raceme), usually; read as {"cyme": "usually"}. The books add head (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 385, 386: cyme, sometimes condensed into heads.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 385, 386, family Cornaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite, usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.

traits.perennation.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cornaceae: how its perennial herbs last from year to year (character 25), coded usually a rhizome. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 25 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.carpels.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family high 4: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 385, 386: 2-4 [-9]. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.
